Glycine receptor antibody-positive progressive encephalomyelitis
with rigidity and myoclonus: A disease with variable clinical
course
P. Vanacker, E. Peeters, M. Schrooten, M. Woodhall, A. Vincent,
W. Vandenberghe (Leuven, Belgium)
Objective: To add to the clinical spectrum of glycine receptor
antibody (GlyR Ab)-positive progressive encephalomyelitis with ri-
gidity and myoclonus (PERM).
Background: PERM is a subacute disorder characterized by rigid-
ity, painful spasms, brainstem dysfunction (including brainstem myo-
clonus), long tract signs and dysautonomia. Recently, several PERM
patients were reported to have GlyR Abs.
Methods: We describe the clinical similarities and differences in
2 patients with GlyR Ab-positive PERM.
Results: Patient 1, a 49-year-old man, developed painful spams of
the right leg, left arm stiffness, jerks, trismus, dysarthria, dysphagia,
diplopia, urinary retention and excessive sweating over the course of
1 week. Brain MRI was normal. Surface EMG was consistent with
brainstem myoclonus. CSF analysis showed mild lymphocytic pleo-
cytosis and elevated IgG index. Serum was negative for antibodies
against GAD and amphiphysin, but positive for GlyR Abs. He recov-
ered completely after resection of a thymoma (Clerinx et al., Neurol-
ogy 76, 303-4, 2011). Patient 2, a 37-year-old man, was admitted
with stiffness, jerks, trismus, dysphagia, diplopia, urinary retention
and gait problems. Clinical exam showed generalized rigidity and
myoclonus, supranuclear upward gaze palsy, slowed saccades and
bilateral Babinski signs. Over the preceding 10 months he had been
hospitalized twice elsewhere with similar symptoms, which had par-
tially and transiently resolved with IV corticosteroids. Brain MRI
was normal. Surface EMG was indicative of brainstem myoclonus.
CSF analysis showed mild lymphocytic pleocytosis and 7 extra oligo-
clonal bands. No tumor was found. Antibodies against GAD and
amphiphysin were negative, but GlyR Abs were positive in serum
and CSF. He is treated with plasma exchange and corticosteroids at
the time of abstract submission.
Conclusions: Both patients with GlyR Ab-positive PERM had
muscle stiffness, brainstem myoclonus, trismus, diplopia, dysphagia
and urinary retention. However, patient 1 had a monophasic illness
that completely resolved after resection of a thymoma, while patient
2 had a relapsing-remitting course and no detectable tumor.
